  "concordance_definition": "The study evaluated the life cycle of translational research for medical interventions, focusing on the time from initial discovery to a highly cited clinical study showing effectiveness. It assessed whether these highly cited interventions were later replicated, remained unchallenged, contradicted, or found to have initially stronger effects in subsequent studies.",
  "limitations_stated": [
    "Highly cited status does not necessarily mean that these interventions continue to be considered as effective as proposed in the original highly cited papers.",
    "Several blockbusters may go through an industrial discovery-testing-production process that does not involve any particular highly cited paper in the peer-reviewed literature.",
    "Claims for large benefits from old interventions require extra caution as they are likely to be exaggerated.",
    "New drug discovery is probably essential for common diseases where the existing drug armamentarium has been already extensively screened.",
    "For uncommon and neglected diseases, the existing drug options may remain largely untested, and old drugs may find interesting new uses."
  ],
  "funding_conflict": null,
  "key_numbers": [
    "Of 101 very promising claims of new discoveries with clear clinical potential made between 1979 and 1983, only five resulted in interventions with licensed clinical use by 2003 and only one had extensive clinical use.",
    "Median translation lag was 24 years (IQR, 14 to 44 years) between first description and earliest highly cited article.",
    "Median translation lag was 44 years for refuted interventions vs. 17 years for nonrefuted ones (P = 0.004).",
    "Median translation lag was 27 years (IQR, 21 to 50 years) when considering the wider class of agents.",
    "For 18 nonrefuted interventions with a highly cited randomized trial, median translation lag was 16.5 years (range 4 to 50 years).",
    "Indinavir and abciximab had the fastest successful translation, taking 4 years from patenting to publication of a highly cited randomized trial.",
    "Range for time from first discovery to first human use was 0 to 28 years.",
    "Range for time from first discovery to first specific human use was 0 to 221 years.",
    "By the end of 2006, effectiveness of 19 interventions had been replicated (n=14) or remained unchallenged (n=5).",
    "13 interventions had been contradicted (n=5) or found to have initially stronger effects (n=8)."
  ]
}
